items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition; conventionally associated with the late Warring States/Qin standardization and transmitted in the Han dictionary tradition; this is a modern digital redraw, not a dated artifact
items.tradition: Chinese small seal-script style, identified by Commons as Shuowen seal script
items.caption: A modern redraw of 姐 in the Shuowen seal-script style. The dictionary analyzes it as 女 plus phonetic 且; this image illustrates that transmitted analysis, not an excavated early form.
items.alt: Digital vector rendering of the seal-script form of 姐, showing a 女-like left component and 且-like right component.
items.selection_reason: It is a well-documented and reusable rendering matching the only clearly supported early graphic tradition found in accessible sources. Use as an illustrative reconstruction, not as proof of an oracle-bone or bronze form.
items.rights: Public domain release stated on the Wikimedia Commons file page; attribution appreciated but not required.

limitations.text: The seal-style candidate is a modern digital reconstruction derived from character databases, not a photograph or independently dated artifact; no earlier excavated 姐 glyph was established in the inspected sources.
Exact Unicode Unihan pages could not be inspected, and Xiaoxuetang's queried record rendered only a shell without candidate labels or images in this browsing tool.
